title: Ezekiel Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 17.

questions.question: What did the word of the LORD command Ezekiel to do?
options: Put forth a riddle and speak a parable
questions.correctAnswer: Put forth a riddle and speak a parable
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was commanded to put forth a riddle and speak a parable unto the house of Israel (Ezekiel 17:2).

questions.question: What did the first great eagle take from the cedar?
questions.explanation: The eagle took the highest branch of the cedar as stated in Ezekiel 17:3.

questions.question: Where did the eagle carry the top of the young twigs?
questions.explanation: The eagle cropped off the top of the young twigs and carried it into a land of traffick, setting it in a city of merchants (Ezekiel 17:4).

questions.question: What type of tree was the seed planted as?
questions.explanation: The seed was planted in a fruitful field and set as a willow tree (Ezekiel 17:5).

questions.question: What did the vine bring forth?
questions.explanation: The vine grew and brought forth branches (Ezekiel 17:6).

questions.question: True or False: The vine's roots were under the eagle.
questions.explanation: The roots of the vine were under the eagle, as mentioned in Ezekiel 17:6.

questions.question: What did the second great eagle possess?
questions.explanation: There was another great eagle with great wings and many feathers (Ezekiel 17:7).

questions.question: True or False: The vine shot forth its branches toward the second eagle.
questions.explanation: The vine shot forth her branches toward the second eagle that might water it (Ezekiel 17:7).

questions.question: What was the purpose of being planted in good soil by great waters?
questions.explanation: It was planted in good soil by great waters to bring forth branches and bear fruit (Ezekiel 17:8).

questions.question: In Ezekiel 17, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: The vine grew and became a spreading vine
The eagle took the highest branch of the cedar
The word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel
The seed was planted in a fruitful field
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel
questions.explanation: The very first instruction is that the word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel (Ezekiel 17:1).

questions.question: True or False: The vine was planted to be a goodly vine.
questions.explanation: The vine was intended to be a goodly vine by being planted in good soil (Ezekiel 17:8).

questions.question: What did the eagle do with the young twigs?
questions.explanation: The eagle cropped off the top of his young twigs (Ezekiel 17:4).

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 17:9, what is suggested will happen to the vine if its roots are pulled up and its fruit is cut off?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:9 states that if the roots are pulled up and the fruit cut off, it shall wither, emphasizing the importance of strong roots for survival.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 17:10 imply about the fate of the vine when the east wind touches it?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:10 states that when the east wind touches it, it shall wither, indicating the vulnerability of the vine to harsh conditions.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 17:12, who is referred to as having been taken along with the king to Babylon?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:12 mentions that the king of Babylon took the king and the princes of Jerusalem with him to Babylon.

questions.question: What is the consequence of breaking the covenant as stated in Ezekiel 17:16?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:16 declares that the king who despised the oath and broke the covenant will die in Babylon, signifying the seriousness of covenant fidelity.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 17:14, why was the kingdom made base?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:14 explains that the kingdom was made base so that it might stand by keeping the covenant, highlighting the importance of obedience.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 17:19 states that the Lord will not recompense the broken covenant upon the king's head.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:19 states that the Lord will recompense upon the king's head for despising His oath and breaking the covenant, indicating that consequences for disobedience are certain.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 17:15 relate to the theme of rebellion against authority?
options: It highlights the consequences of rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the consequences of rebellion
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:15 discusses the king's rebellion in sending ambassadors to Egypt, questioning whether he shall prosper or escape, emphasizing the dangers of rebellion against God's authority.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 17:21 states that all the trees of the field will know the Lord's actions.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:21 mentions that all the trees of the field shall know that the Lord has spoken, indicating that God's actions are recognized by all creation.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 17:13 indicate about the king's seed and the covenant made?
options: It was taken and an oath was made
questions.correctAnswer: It was taken and an oath was made
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:13 describes how the king of Babylon took of the king's seed and made a covenant with him, demonstrating the political and spiritual dynamics at play.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 17:8, where was the vine planted?
options: In a good soil by great waters
questions.correctAnswer: In a good soil by great waters
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:8 states that the vine was planted in a good soil by great waters, emphasizing the ideal conditions for growth.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 17:24 illustrate God's sovereignty over nations?
options: By drying up the green tree
By bringing down the high tree
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:24 shows God's sovereignty by stating He has brought down the high tree, exalted the low tree, dried up the green tree, and made the dry tree to flourish.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 17:20 describes the Lord spreading His net upon the king as a means of deliverance.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:20 explains that the Lord will spread His net upon the king, indicating a trap rather than deliverance, showing the consequences of rebellion.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 17.

questions.question: What did the great eagle take from the cedar in Lebanon?
questions.explanation: The great eagle took the highest branch of the cedar as stated in Ezekiel 17:3.

questions.question: In what kind of land did the eagle plant the seed?
questions.explanation: The eagle planted the seed in a fruitful field according to Ezekiel 17:5.

questions.question: What does the vine symbolize in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The vine represents Israel, as it is the subject of God's communication through Ezekiel, especially in the context of rebellion against Babylon's king.

questions.question: What will happen to the king who despised the oath and broke the covenant?
questions.explanation: As stated in Ezekiel 17:16, the king will die in the place where he broke the covenant.

questions.question: What does God say He will spread upon the king as a consequence of his actions?
questions.explanation: God states in Ezekiel 17:20 that He will spread His net upon him, indicating capture and judgment.

questions.question: True or False: The king will receive help from Pharaoh in the war.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:17 states that Pharaoh with his army will not aid the king in war, indicating his isolation.

questions.question: What will happen to the fugitives and bands of the king?
options: They will fall by the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They will fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:21 says that all his fugitives and bands shall fall by the sword as a consequence of rebellion.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominent in Ezekiel 17 regarding the fate of the high and low trees?
questions.explanation: The high and low trees symbolize the rise and fall of powers, reflecting God's sovereignty and judgment as seen in Ezekiel 17:24.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 17:23 promise about the new planting in Israel?
options: It will be a goodly cedar
It will be destroyed by the east wind
questions.correctAnswer: It will be a goodly cedar
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:23 promises that the new planting will bring forth boughs and be a goodly cedar.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage discusses the consequences of breaking covenants, similar to Ezekiel 17?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11 discusses the consequences of breaking the covenant, similar to the themes in Ezekiel 17.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'covenant' imply about God's promises in Ezekiel 17?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'covenant' indicates that it is conditional upon obedience, as noted in Ezekiel 17:14.

questions.question: True or False: God will make the dry tree to flourish.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:24 confirms that God will make the dry tree to flourish, symbolizing restoration and hope.

questions.question: What is the significance of bringing the high cedar down and exalting the low tree in Ezekiel 17:24?
options: It indicates a change in leadership
It shows the failure of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:24 highlights God's sovereignty in reversing fortunes, signifying His judgment and authority over nations.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 17:3 describe the great eagle doing?
options: Took the highest branch of the cedar
questions.correctAnswer: Took the highest branch of the cedar
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:3 states, 'A great eagle...came unto Lebanon, and took the highest branch of the cedar,' showing the eagle's authority and purpose in the parable.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 17:9, what question does the Lord pose about the vine's prosperity?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:9 asks, 'Shall it prosper?' indicating God's inquiry into the fate of the vine, reflecting His sovereignty over the situation.

questions.question: What does the second eagle symbolize in Ezekiel 17:7?
questions.explanation: The second eagle represents Egypt, as indicated by the vine bending towards it for water, which signifies reliance on foreign powers contrary to God's will (Ezekiel 17:7).

questions.question: What covenant does the king of Babylon make according to Ezekiel 17:13?
options: A covenant with the king's seed
questions.correctAnswer: A covenant with the king's seed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:13 states that the king of Babylon 'hath taken of the king's seed, and made a covenant with him,' indicating a political alliance meant to stabilize his rule.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 17:24, what does God declare about the trees of the field?
options: They will know the Lord's actions
questions.correctAnswer: They will know the Lord's actions
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:24 reveals that 'all the trees of the field shall know that I the LORD have brought down the high tree,' illustrating God's sovereignty and authority over nations.

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized in Ezekiel 17:20 regarding judgment?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:20 highlights God's justice as He declares He will 'bring him to Babylon, and will plead with him there for his trespass,' emphasizing accountability for disobedience.

questions.question: What significant action does the king of Babylon take in Ezekiel 17:12?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:12 states that the king of Babylon 'hath taken the king thereof, and the princes thereof,' indicating a significant political move that impacts Israel's leadership.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 17:16, what will happen to the king who breaks the covenant?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:16 declares, 'he shall die,' emphasizing the severe consequences of breaking the covenant with God and the king who made him king.

questions.question: What does the imagery of the vine in Ezekiel 17:6 convey about Israel's relationship with God?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:6 describes the vine's growth and its roots under the eagle, symbolizing Israel's dependency on God for sustenance and support.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 17:15 highlight the theme of rebellion?
options: By stating he rebelled against Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: By stating he rebelled against Babylon
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:15 notes that the king 'rebelled against him in sending his ambassadors into Egypt,' illustrating the theme of rebellion against the divinely ordained authority.

questions.question: What does God declare about His oath in Ezekiel 17:19?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:19 states, 'as I live, surely mine oath that he hath despised...even it will I recompense upon his own head,' indicating God's commitment to uphold His word.

questions.question: What lesson about leadership can be drawn from Ezekiel 17:14 regarding the king's covenant?
options: Leadership is maintained through faithfulness to covenants
questions.correctAnswer: Leadership is maintained through faithfulness to covenants
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:14 indicates the importance of maintaining the covenant, stating 'that the kingdom might be base...that by keeping of his covenant it might stand.'

questions.question: In the context of Ezekiel 17, what does the 'east wind' represent in Ezekiel 17:10?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:10 mentions that when the east wind touches the vine, 'it shall wither,' indicating the destructive forces that can impact Israel due to disobedience.

questions.question: What does the setting of the vine near great waters in Ezekiel 17:5 suggest about God's provision?
options: God provides only for the strong
God's provision is abundant and nurturing
God's provision is conditional on obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God's provision is abundant and nurturing
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:5 describes the vine being planted 'by great waters,' showcasing God's abundant provision and nurturing care for His people.
